title: TWC 2026 research ledger
purpose: Sixty pre-event research entries checked against public sources before being published (20 from the first pass and 20 from the second pass, both Sept 23, 2026; 20 from the third pass, Sept 24, 2026). This is a dated snapshot, not a live feed.
method: Each claim is checked line-by-line against the linked public source text or structured record before it is added; every entry carries at least one review URL. Five passes of 20 entries: passes 1-2 on Sept 23, passes 3-4 on Sept 24 (entries 1-80), pass 5 on Sept 24 (entries 81-100: FISSURE Playground 3 results and interviews, molodoy's eye condition, StarSeries MVP/EVPs, the PGL Masters Bucharest qualifier field, the 2027 Major/EWC calendar, the Americas VRS race, org closures, Virtus.pro's VRS trajectory, and 3-month map-pool win rates for all eight teams). Source conflicts and moving rankings stay visible; see the Irregularities section of master-list.html.

entries.claim: The TWC 2026 Finals are scheduled for October 14–18, 2026 at BLAST Studios Malta with a $1,000,000 Finals prize pool.
entries.detail: The event is the fourth edition; GAM3RS_X is the organizer and GRID is the data partner.

entries.claim: The full 2026 circuit is advertised at $1,115,000 and consists of five regional online series, a Global Qualifier and the Finals.
entries.detail: The published series amounts are EU1 $30,000, EU2 $30,000, NA $15,000, SA1 $20,000 and SA2 $20,000, plus the $1,000,000 Finals.

entries.claim: The Finals format is two four-team GSL groups with Bo3 matches, followed by a single-elimination playoff; the Grand Final is Bo5 and a third-place decider is listed.
entries.detail: The event page lists a $500,000 player share and a $500,000 club share. It does not mean the Finals prize pool is $500,000.

entries.claim: The eight-team Finals field was announced on September 16, 2026: Falcons, 9z, Legacy, FURIA, BETBOOM, Aurora, PARIVISION and Virtus.pro.
entries.detail: The first seven entered through the VRS invite route; Virtus.pro entered through the closed qualifier.

entries.claim: The direct-invite basis is Valve's official Global VRS snapshot dated August 3, 2026.
entries.detail: At that snapshot the Finals teams were Falcons #2, 9z #4, Legacy #7, FURIA #8, BetBoom #9, Aurora #10, PARIVISION #12 and Virtus.pro #37.

entries.claim: Virtus.pro won the September 9–13 Global Qualifier and took the last Finals place.
entries.detail: VP lost the opener to K27, then recovered through BESTIA, a K27 rematch and playoff wins over FOKUS, HEROIC and HOTU. The Grand Final against HOTU was a 3–0 Bo5, with maps Dust II 16–14, Anubis 13–6 and Ancient 16–13; the linked coverage and match record agree.

entries.claim: Falcons replaced benched IGL kyxsan with karrigan from FaZe on April 20, 2026.
entries.detail: HLTV says karrigan reunited with NiKo and coach zonic and took over leadership after Falcons placed third at IEM Rio.

entries.claim: Falcons won IEM Cologne Major 2026 3–0 over FURIA; m0NESY received the ESL Pro Tour DHL MVP award.
entries.detail: ESL's official release also reports the event's viewership record and Falcons' first Major title. The record claim is kept separate from performance analysis.

entries.claim: FalleN announced on the IEM Rio stage that he plans to retire at the end of 2026.
entries.detail: This is a reported player statement and a tournament storyline, not a claim that he will leave FURIA before TWC.

entries.claim: molodoy was ranked sixth in HLTV's 2025 top-20 and named Rookie of the Year.
entries.detail: This is historical player context; it is not a TWC 2026 event statistic.

entries.claim: Legacy replaced lux with arT in early February 2026.
entries.detail: HLTV reports the benching on February 2 and arT's signing from Fluxo on February 3; the site's claim is limited to those roster actions.

entries.claim: Legacy signed try from Imperial in July 2026, with saadzin moving the other way; n1ssim also returned to the active lineup.
entries.detail: The two transactions are separate HLTV reports and are not combined into a claim about tactical quality.

entries.claim: Legacy won FISSURE Playground 3 on September 13, 2026 with a 3–0 final against G2; latto was the final's MVP.
entries.detail: HLTV reports latto's final line as 69–34, 102.9 ADR, 80.6% KAST and 1.67 Rating 3.0. This is a single final, not a season average.

entries.claim: Aurora's current Finals five followed a July 2026 rebuild: kyxsan, XANTARES, woxic, Wicadia and Jimpphat, coached by ash/ashhh in the linked reports.
entries.detail: The roster turnover and dates are sourced; labels such as 'favorite' or 'new-coach bounce' remain analysis, not facts.

entries.claim: 9z's current five is max, dgt, meyern, luchov and HUASOPEEK; the August 3 VRS snapshot had 9z fourth globally.
entries.detail: The roster history includes luchov and meyern joining, Luken leaving and dgt returning. HLTV's September 21 ranking is a separate snapshot and places 9z #16.

entries.claim: BetBoom's Finals five is Boombl4, zorte, S1ren, d1Ledez and Magnojez after the FL4MUS loan/stand-in period ended.
entries.detail: The site distinguishes a temporary LAN stand-in from the registered Finals roster; a visa problem in spring 2026 is not evidence of a current problem. Pass-3 correction: FL4MUS replaced d1Ledez at IEM Atlanta; at the Cologne Major the absent player was S1ren (see entry 57).

entries.claim: PARIVISION's last pre-event move was to bench slaxejezzz and return HObbit to the active lineup on September 17, 2026; FL1T remains in the five.
entries.detail: This change happened after the eight-team announcement. HObbit's original stand-in spell and FL1T's July replacement are recorded as separate changes.

entries.claim: Virtus.pro completed a 2026 rebuild with mir, b1st, F0R3VER, AquaRS and tO0RO, coached by ProbLeM.
entries.detail: HLTV reports Perfecto, FL1T and fame being removed from the active roster and the academy promotions of AquaRS and F0R3VER after mir's return.

entries.claim: Valve's July 8, 2026 update added Cache to the Active Duty map pool and removed Overpass; TWC's event page lists Cache, Dust II, Mirage, Inferno, Nuke, Ancient and Anubis.
entries.detail: The official update is the date authority. Third-party July 6 publication dates are flagged rather than used.

entries.claim: TWC sits in the run-up to the PGL Major Singapore 2026, listed for November 25–December 13 with 32 teams and a $1.25 million prize pool.
entries.detail: The Singapore venue page is an external event listing; the VRS cutoff and invitations can change, so this is context rather than a qualification guarantee for any TWC team.

entries.claim: FURIA are the defending Thunderpick World Championship titleholders: they won TWC 2025 with a 3-2 reverse sweep over NAVI in Malta (final played October 19, 2025).
entries.detail: NAVI led 2-0 (Mirage 13-6, Inferno) before FURIA won Nuke, Dust2 and the decider 13-1. KSCERATO earned his first Grand Final MVP. Prize places: FURIA $500,000; NAVI $150,000; The MongolZ $70,000; Aurora $50,000; Venom/9z/Imperial/OG $20,000 each.

entries.claim: TWC roll of honour: 2023 FaZe (beat Virtus.pro, ropz MVP), 2024 The MongolZ (beat HEROIC 3-1 in Berlin on November 3, 2024), 2025 FURIA.
entries.detail: The 2024 edition ran October 21 - November 3 with 16 teams and an $850,000 total prize pool ($500,000 to The MongolZ; 3DMAX third). The 2023 first edition was a $500,000 event won by FaZe Clan.

entries.claim: The five 2026 regional series winners were: DragonClaw (EU Series 1, 2-1 over TDK), M80 (North America, 2-0 over Wildcard), ShindeN (South America Series 1, over UNO MILLE), Imperial (South America Series 2, 2-0 over BESTIA) and GenOne (EU Series 2, over Lazer Cats).
entries.detail: EU Series 1 final May 31; NA final May 3 (only two of seven playoff series were actually played - the rest were forfeits by teams unable to field eligible lineups); SA1 June 28; SA2 July 12; EU2 August 2. None of the five winners reached the Finals field - the Finals places came via VRS invites and the Global Qualifier.

entries.claim: VRSDelivery renamed to DragonClaw on May 30, 2026 - one day before winning TWC EU Series 1 - which is why the winner appears under two names across sources.
entries.detail: Hotspawn's May 31 final report says 'VRSDelivery'; HLTV's event prize list says 'DragonClaw' (Poland). Liquipedia's EU Series 1 page carries the note 'May 30th - VRSDelivery rename to DragonClaw.' Both names refer to the same team. (Liquipedia also logs a June 2 DragonClaw disqualification from a different event, European Pro League Series 7, pending an organizer investigation - unrelated to TWC.)

entries.claim: Six players from the TWC 2026 Finals field made HLTV's Top 20 players of 2025: m0NESY #4, molodoy #6, KSCERATO #9, XANTARES #14, YEKINDAR #15, NiKo #18.
entries.detail: The full top three were ZywOo #1, donk #2, ropz #3. Falcons and FURIA each placed two players inside the top ten of the year.

entries.claim: NiKo's #18 placing in 2025 was his record tenth career appearance in HLTV's Top 20 - the most of any player.
entries.detail: HLTV: 'NiKo sets a new record for most Top 20 appearances (ten) as he takes the 18th spot in the 2025 ranking.'

entries.claim: m0NESY's #4 in 2025 was his fourth consecutive Top 20 placing (7th in 2022, 4th in 2023, 2nd in 2024, 4th in 2025), in the first year of his career without a trophy.
entries.detail: HLTV also records that G2 signed him from NAVI in 2022 for a reported $600,000 when he was 16 years old. He moved from G2 to Falcons in April 2025.

entries.claim: karrigan left FaZe for Falcons on April 20, 2026 after a five-year second stint (February 2021 - April 2026) that had delivered FaZe's first Major (PGL Major Antwerp 2022, the first Major ever won by an international roster), eight LAN titles and the Intel Grand Slam Season 4.
entries.detail: The move was first reported by KRL on April 12; Twistzz told fans karrigan 'wasn't kicked' and the move was sudden. karrigan (born April 14, 1990) reunited with NiKo and coach zonic; FaZe had just missed the IEM Cologne Major for the first time in the organization's history. He won the Cologne Major with Falcons 61 days after joining.

entries.claim: The IEM Cologne Major 2026 grand final set multiple records: NiKo lifted his first Major 3,067 days after ELEAGUE Boston 2018, karrigan won his second, and zonic his record sixth as a coach (four with Astralis, one with Vitality, one with Falcons).
entries.detail: All three final maps vs FURIA ended 13-8 (Mirage, Anubis, Inferno). karrigan joined apEX, b1t, ropz and ZywOo as the only players to win Majors in both CS:GO and CS2; it was a first Major for m0NESY, TeSeS and kyousuke. Falcons earned $500,000.

entries.claim: Falcons' only tier-one title before karrigan arrived was PGL Bucharest 2025 (April 13, 2025, 3-0 over G2, with degster as MVP); after m0NESY joined they then lost seven consecutive grand finals.
entries.detail: The lost finals with m0NESY pre-karrigan: IEM Melbourne 2025, BLAST Rivals Spring 2025, Esports World Cup 2025, ESL Pro League Season 22, IEM Chengdu 2025, BLAST Rivals Fall 2025 and BLAST Bounty Winter 2026. (After karrigan joined they also finished 2nd at PGL Astana 2026 and CAC 2026 either side of winning the Cologne Major.)

entries.claim: FURIA won four titles in 2025 - FISSURE Playground 2, the Thunderpick World Championship 2025, IEM Chengdu 2025 and BLAST Rivals Fall 2025 - and closed 2025 as the #1 team in Valve's global standings.
entries.detail: The BLAST Rivals Fall 2025 final (November 16, Hong Kong) was a 3-1 win over Falcons and, per the reported VRS update, lifted FURIA to 1,997 points, #1 in the world.

entries.claim: Falcons won all four of their series against FURIA in 2026: BLAST Open Rotterdam 2-1 (March 23), the IEM Rio third-place decider 2-0 (April 19), the PGL Astana quarterfinal 2-1 (May 15) and the IEM Cologne Major grand final 3-0 (June 21).
entries.detail: FURIA's most recent series win in the pairing was the BLAST Rivals Fall 2025 grand final, 3-1 in Hong Kong on November 16, 2025. At PGL Astana groups, 9z beat Falcons 2-1 (May 10) - a rare 2026 loss for Falcons to a TWC field side.

entries.claim: Aurora's roster core came from Eternal Fire: on April 5, 2025 the organization signed the entire Eternal Fire five (MAJ3R, XANTARES, woxic, Wicadia, jottAAA) plus coach Fabre, after woxic cited unfavourable sponsorship conditions for CS in Turkey.
entries.detail: The all-Turkish era ended on July 2, 2026 when MAJ3R stepped down; the Finals five (kyxsan, XANTARES, woxic, Wicadia, Jimpphat + coach ash) is the international rebuild that followed.

entries.claim: Boombl4 is a PGL Major Stockholm 2021 champion with NAVI (also IEM Cologne 2021 and two BLAST Premier Finals that year) who joined BetBoom in January 2025.
entries.detail: At the IEM Cologne Major 2026 he led BetBoom from Stage 1 into the playoffs while playing with a stand-in (FL4MUS), their first Major playoff appearance of the era.

entries.claim: Jame won the IEM Rio Major 2022 with Outsiders (Virtus.pro competing under a neutral name), beating HEROIC 2-0 in the final, and was named HLTV MVP of the event with a 1.30 rating.
entries.detail: Jame now plays for PARIVISION together with Rio-winning teammates FL1T and coach dastan. Virtus.pro's own profile page confirms Jame as a former captain of the VP roster and Rio 2022 champion and MVP.

entries.claim: BetBoom's 2026 visa saga reshaped the Finals five: on March 23 FL4MUS and zorte stood in for visa-hit d1Ledez AND ArtFr0st for three LANs; on April 9 d1Ledez returned, zorte was kept for the season and ArtFr0st was benched; on August 1 ArtFr0st was loaned to 1win as TDK's core moved there.
entries.detail: BetBoom stated ArtFr0st 'needed to apply for a US visa from Europe, but without a Schengen visa, he automatically lost the opportunity to participate in the Atlanta tournament.' The TDK-to-1win transfer also made Ax1Le's move permanent (from the BetBoom bench) and loaned PARIVISION's BELCHONOKK to 1win. ArtFr0st had himself joined BetBoom permanently from PARIVISION in February 2026.

entries.claim: CS2's competitive format is MR12: 12 rounds per half, first team to 13 wins, maximum 24 regulation rounds; overtime is MR3 (first to 4 OT rounds); rounds last 1:55 with a 40-second bomb timer. At TWC 2026 overtime starts with $12,500 (rulebook 4.1).
entries.detail: Corrected in pass 3: the earlier '$10,000 at Valve Majors' overtime figure was not supported by Valve's Major rulebook (which only requires Premier default settings) and has been removed; see entry 43. Matchmaking games can end 12-12 as draws, but pro matches always play overtime to a winner.

entries.claim: Valve's Regional Standings (VRS) rank teams from prize money earned, beaten opponents' prize money and count of teams beaten, plus head-to-head results; HLTV's implementation shows the formula: a 400-point base plus up to 1,600 points scaled across four factors (bounty offered, bounty collected, opponent network, LAN wins) with head-to-head adjustments.
entries.detail: Points are age-weighted and decay over roughly six months; standings belong to a five-player roster, not an organization. Valve's August 2025 model update added a minimum participation requirement (5 of the last 10 matches) for a player to appear on a roster's VRS entry and let connected stages (qualifiers/group stages) count a share of the final stage's prize pool. Snapshots exclude matches from events that had not completed by the snapshot date.

entries.claim: TWC 2025 set the Thunderpick series' viewership record, with a 62% increase over the 2024 championship finals.
entries.detail: Per Thunderpick's official release distributed by PRNewswire/Morningstar, Oct 27, 2025.

entries.claim: Legacy have won three titles in China within roughly twelve months - CAC 2025, CAC 2026 (3-1 over Falcons in Shanghai, May 24, 2026) and FISSURE Playground 3 (September 13, 2026) - with latto named MVP at all three.
entries.detail: In the CAC 2026 final Legacy lost Nuke 1-13 then won three straight maps; kyousuke (1.28) and TeSeS (1.62) ratings could not save Falcons. latto's FISSURE final: 1.67 rating, 102.9 ADR, 80.6% KAST. latto finished in HLTV's top 30 for 2025 and targets a first top-20 placing in 2026 (two MVPs + two EVPs this year at the time of the FISSURE final).

entries.claim: Core-roster rule: every Finals team must field at least three of the five players on its roster in Valve's August 3, 2026 VRS snapshot, or it faces a technical loss. All eight current Finals fives comply.
entries.detail: Recomputed against Valve's Aug 3 file. Falcons, FURIA, Aurora, 9z and Virtus.pro field 5/5. Legacy (saadzin → try), BetBoom (FL4MUS → S1ren) and PARIVISION (slaxejezzz → FL1T) field 4/5. For those three teams, one more lineup change still leaves 3/5; a second change would breach the rule.

entries.claim: Roster rules: a team may register at most 8 members (the coach may act as a stand-in). One stand-in may be used; the stand-in must be registered 72 hours in advance and approved 15 minutes before the match. An emergency stand-in may be kept confidential.
entries.detail: Rulebook sections 3.5 and 3.7/3.7.1. Betting consequence: a late emergency stand-in may not be public until very close to the match, so prices can move late.

entries.claim: Server settings are MR12 with $800 start money, 1:55 rounds, 20-second freeze time, a 40-second bomb and three 30-second tactical timeouts per team. Overtime is MR3 (best of 6) with $12,500 starting money and one timeout per overtime.
entries.detail: Rulebook section 4.1. This replaces entry 37's unverified '$10,000 at Valve Majors' overtime claim. Valve's Major supplemental rulebook only says servers use Premier defaults and gives no dollar figure.

entries.claim: Map veto is run on Discord after a coin toss decides Team A and Team B. Bo3 order: A ban, B ban, A pick, B pick, A ban, B ban; the remaining map is the decider, with sides chosen by knife round. Bo5 order: A ban, B ban, then four alternating picks; knife round for the decider.
entries.detail: Rulebook section 4.4. The seven-map pool in section 4.3 (Inferno, Nuke, Dust2, Ancient, Mirage, Cache, Anubis) matches the HLTV and Liquipedia event pages.

entries.claim: Delay and pause rules: in a Bo3, a team 15 minutes late forfeits map 1 and a team 30 minutes late forfeits the series. Technical pauses have time limits. A team that loses a player may continue 4v5 if it has won 10 or more rounds or leads by 6 or more.
entries.detail: Rulebook sections 3.17.2 and 3.17.3. These rules matter for settlement: check each bookmaker's rules on forfeits and walkovers.

entries.claim: Withdrawal replacement rule: a team that withdraws more than 20 days before the event is replaced by the next team in the VRS; a withdrawal less than 20 days out is filled by the next European VRS team. Invited teams had 72 hours to accept.
entries.detail: Rulebook sections 2.4.5 and 2.4.6. Counting back 20 days from the October 14 start gives about September 24, so any late replacement now comes from Europe (date arithmetic is our inference).

entries.claim: Integrity and payout rules: players and staff are banned from betting (section 2.9); prize money is paid November 1-15 (section 2.7); anti-cheat is Akros (section 4.5.5). Three minor violations count as one major, and three majors mean disqualification (sections 5.1-5.2).
entries.detail: From the rulebook dated 01.07.2026. The document is titled '[INTERNAL]' and contains stale '2025' wording (flagged as an irregularity).

entries.claim: Seeding uses the September VRS. Valve's September 7, 2026 global snapshot ranks the field as follows: Falcons #3, Legacy #6, FURIA #7, 9z #9, Aurora #12, BetBoom #15, PARIVISION #18, Virtus.pro #40.
entries.detail: The seed order 1-8 in that sequence is our inference from the snapshot. Neither the rulebook nor the official page publishes how seeds map to the two groups, and no draw had been published as of Sept 24.

entries.claim: Travel logistics: the official Finals page says the event is in the Schengen visa area and covers travel and accommodation for up to 7 people per team. Finals week runs from arrival on Oct 12 to departure on Oct 19.
entries.detail: Risk flag: in 2026, visa problems cost BetBoom players European LANs (see entries 36 and 57). No visa problem for TWC has been reported as of Sept 24.

entries.claim: ESL Pro League Season 24 runs October 3-11, 2026 in Katowice: 16 teams, $1,000,000, Swiss stage then an 8-team single-elimination bracket, with the Bo5 final on Oct 11. It includes 7 of the 8 TWC teams. Virtus.pro is the only TWC team not entered.
entries.detail: EPL entrants: 12 teams invited from the Aug 3 VRS, including Falcons, 9z, Legacy, FURIA, BetBoom, Aurora and PARIVISION, plus 4 ESL Challenger League qualifiers (1w Team, M80, ShindeN, TYLOO). The EPL final is one day before TWC arrival (Oct 12) and three days before TWC matches start (Oct 14). This is a fatigue and strat-hiding flag.

entries.claim: fame's path after being transfer-listed by Virtus.pro in February 2026: a loan to K27 from April 22 (originally to the end of May, then extended; HLTV lists it ending July 1), a loan to TDK from July 17, and a permanent move when 1win signed TDK's core on August 1, 2026. Virtus.pro announced the transfer.
entries.detail: 1win (fame, ArtFr0st, Ax1Le, nafany, BELCHONOKK) qualified for EPL S24 through ESL Challenger League Europe. fame is not at TWC.

entries.claim: StarSeries Fall 2026 (Barcelona, Sept 17-20; $500,000 including the club share): Vitality beat Aurora 3-1 in the Bo5 final. Aurora finished 2nd and FURIA 3rd.
entries.detail: Final maps: Anubis 13-4 Vitality, Inferno 13-11 Aurora, Mirage 13-4 Vitality, Cache 13-7 Vitality. This was Vitality's first title since BLAST Rivals on May 3, and ZywOo (1.51 in the final) was MVP. Player-share prizes: $100k / $65k / $35k.

entries.claim: Aurora's StarSeries run went through the upper bracket: 2-0 over NAVI, 2-0 over NRG, then 2-1 over Vitality in the upper final (Sept 19). They lost the grand final rematch 1-3.
entries.detail: Grand-final ratings: Wicadia 1.15, woxic 0.84, kyxsan 0.83, Jimpphat 0.81, XANTARES 0.69. The final loss came with XANTARES quiet (0.69).

entries.claim: FURIA at StarSeries: they beat MIBR 2-1, then lost 0-2 to Vitality, then won 2-1 over MOUZ and 2-0 over MIBR, then lost 0-2 to Vitality again in the consolidation final, finishing 3rd.
entries.detail: FURIA went 0-4 on maps against Vitality at the event. HLTV had FURIA #4 (Sept 14 ranking).

entries.claim: YEKINDAR said on Sept 17 that he is no longer calling: he handed the T-side calling he had taken on Anubis, Cache and Ancient back to FalleN, calling the load 'too much cortisol'.
entries.detail: FalleN, who retires at the end of 2026, is again FURIA's sole caller. HLTV notes his rating was 0.90 over 48 maps in the last three months. This affects TWC map-level reads for FURIA on those three maps.

entries.claim: BLAST Open Porto 2026 (Aug 26-Sep 6, $1.1M): Spirit beat MOUZ 3-1. TWC teams: Falcons 3rd-4th (lost to MOUZ 1-2 in the group upper final, beat G2 2-0, lost to Spirit 0-2 in the semi-final); FURIA 5th-6th (lost to Spirit 0-2 and Vitality 1-2); Aurora and Legacy were eliminated in the groups (Aurora 1-2 vs G2; Legacy 1-2 vs Vitality).
entries.detail: HLTV's final report describes 'Falcons struggling to repeat their Major glory'. Spirit and MOUZ, the two finalists, are not at TWC.

entries.claim: Correction: BetBoom's lineups changed between events. At IEM Atlanta (May 12-17) FL4MUS replaced d1Ledez. At the IEM Cologne Major (June 2-18) d1Ledez played and S1ren missed the event, with FL4MUS as the fifth.
entries.detail: Valve's Aug 3 match-level data shows these five-man lineups per match. The site previously said FL4MUS deputized for d1Ledez during the Cologne Major; that is corrected on all pages. HLTV reported S1ren would miss the start of the Cologne Major.

entries.claim: Valve's CS2 update of Sept 22, 2026 added a silent (but slower) reload by holding the reload key, made unscoping a sniper silent, fixed geometry on Ancient, Cache and Mirage, and made 'Dynamic Quad' the default crosshair.
entries.detail: This is the last known gameplay patch before TWC. Silent reloads and unscopes change sound information in clutches and for AWPers; expect teams to adapt during EPL. The CS2 update is listed in Valve's official update feed.

entries.claim: PGL Major Singapore invitations use the Valve VRS published on November 2, 2026. Only one other regular snapshot (October 5) falls before that cutoff, and TWC (Oct 14-18) is played inside that window.
entries.detail: PGL announced the cutoff on April 9, 2026. Sources disagree on the Major's start date (Nov 24 in PGL press releases, Nov 25 on the event page); flagged as an irregularity. Whether TWC results carry VRS weight follows Valve's standard method (inference: Valve-eligible LAN results count).

entries.claim: Magisk (Falcons bench) was benched on June 23, 2025 and replaced by kyousuke. On June 30, 2026 BC.Game signed him as in-game leader alongside s1mple, electroNic and Senzu; mzinho completed the roster on July 9.
entries.detail: BC.Game is not in the TWC field. This replaces the site's earlier vague 'later listed with BC.Game' note with dated sources.

entries.claim: Global Qualifier structure: 16 slots (14 Europe VRS invites, 1 North America and 1 South America Americas-VRS invite), 4 GSL groups of four feeding an 8-team single-elimination playoff, Bo3 throughout except a Bo5 Grand Final; played online in Europe on September 9–13 (groups 9–11, playoffs 12–13).
entries.detail: Invites used the August 3 VRS publication. HLTV labels the top-eight playoff bracket the 'Play-in'. The official page's '8 Teams advance to Group Stage' line appears to be a typo for advancing to the playoffs (the playoff bracket is 8 teams).

entries.claim: Global Qualifier final placings: 1st Virtus.pro (qualified for the Finals), 2nd HOTU, 3rd–4th HEROIC and BBL, 5th–8th 1win, 100 Thieves, Wildcard, FOKUS, 9th–12th Ninjas in Pyjamas, 3DMAX, Nemesis, K27, 13th–16th INFINITE, Acend, EYEBALLERS, BESTIA.
entries.detail: Only the winner advanced. Cross-checked against esportsinsider's standings table (win-loss records: VP 5–1 down to 0–2 for the bottom four) and its partial results feed — both agree with HLTV's prize list.

entries.claim: 100 Thieves fielded Major champions Nicolai 'device' Reedtz and Håvard 'rain' Nygaard at the Global Qualifier (with Gizmy, poiii and sirah) and were eliminated in the quarterfinals, 0–2 by HOTU, finishing 5th–8th.
entries.detail: HLTV's HOTU–100 Thieves match page lists the five-man lineup and the 2–0 scoreline (Anubis 13–8, Mirage 13–9 per the half records). Two decorated names' return to CS2 did not reach the Malta Finals.

entries.claim: Official-source contradiction: the Global Qualifier page says ‘Four teams will earn a slot in the TWC Finals’, but the same page says ‘The winner of the Global Qualifier earns a spot’ — and in fact only Virtus.pro qualified.
entries.detail: Flagged as irregularity #18. The result record confirms a single slot; the ‘four teams’ sentence appears to be stale template text. Reviewers can verify both lines on the linked official page.

entries.claim: Qualifier seeding and logistics: invites came from the August VRS but ‘Initial Seed VRS: September VRS’; teams had to be physically based in Europe for the full event; only Americas VRS invitees received travel and accommodation (6 pax), arriving September 7 and departing September 14.
entries.detail: The page does not name which two teams held the Americas slots — that mapping is not published (minor gap, flagged). Useful for reading stand-in and latency context in the qualifier results.

entries.claim: The Global Qualifier carried no prize money — HLTV's prize distribution is ‘Spot at Main Event’ only; the sole reward for the 16-team field was the Finals slot.
entries.detail: Contrast with the regional series, which paid $15k–$30k each (entry 2).

entries.claim: Headliners absent from the Finals: HLTV's top three on Sept 21 (Spirit, Vitality, MOUZ) plus NAVI and G2 are all missing; FURIA and Falcons are the only top-five teams in the field, and four teams are top-10 (FURIA #4, Falcons #5, Legacy #6, Aurora #9 on HLTV's Sept 21 ranking).
entries.detail: esportbet (Sept 16) called FURIA and Falcons ‘the only two top-five ranked teams’; esports.net (Sept 17), citing Sport.ua and HLTV, reported NAVI, G2, Spirit, MOUZ and Vitality all missing. Field-strength context for outright pricing — the draw is materially weaker than a Major.

entries.claim: FURIA are the only past TWC champion in the 2026 field: 2023 winners FaZe and 2024 winners The MongolZ did not qualify, and 2025 runner-up NAVI is absent as well; the roll of honour has never had a repeat winner.
entries.detail: Verified against the announced eight-team field (HLTV/PRNewswire Sept 16) and the past-winners record (2023 FaZe, 2024 The MongolZ, 2025 FURIA — three different organizations). The MongolZ returned in 2025 as defending champions and finished 3rd ($70,000). No organization has won the title twice.

entries.claim: In July 2026 The MongolZ — the 2024 TWC champions, absent from the 2026 Finals — signed 17-year-old tikuak (from Chinggis Warriors) and 18-year-old academy graduate DarkMeister after benching cobrazera and losing mzinho to BC.Game.
entries.detail: Ecosystem watch: The MongolZ remain Asia's top team and a Singapore Major seeding bellwether; their roster state affects the Major race that TWC's VRS points feed.

entries.claim: On September 15, 2026 The MongolZ benched both tikuak and DarkMeister — two months after signing them — leaving three active players (bLitz, Techno, 910) plus coach maaRaa in the middle of the Major race.
entries.detail: The organisation confirmed on X (@1mongolz, Sept 15); shanethegamer (Sept 16) notes they now have as many benched as active players. Flagged as ecosystem drama: an incomplete roster near the November 2 VRS cutoff can alter Singapore Major pools and PGL Bucharest opponents.

entries.claim: PARIVISION's HObbit is a PGL Major Kraków 2017 champion with Gambit (born 1994, ~$884,000 career winnings) and had already been a PARIVISION stand-in from June 17 to July 29, 2026 before re-signing on September 17.
entries.detail: Liquipedia's player page supports the pedigree and the exact stand-in window. This sharpens the site's earlier 're-signed' shorthand: his status has changed three times since June (stand-in Jun 17, out Jul 29, permanent Sep 17).

entries.claim: PGL Masters Bucharest (Oct 24–31, PGL Studio, Bucharest) is a 16-team, $1,250,000 Valve Tier 1 event: Bo3 Swiss stage into a single-elimination playoff with a Bo5 final; invites were issued from the July 6 VRS and main-event seeding uses the October 5 VRS.
entries.detail: Prize split is again 50/50 players/clubs ($625,000 each). It is the last Tier-1 stop before the November 2 VRS cutoff for PGL Major Singapore — and the Oct 5 seeding snapshot is the one TWC results can move (entry 59).

entries.claim: Five of the eight TWC teams are in Bucharest's announced 12-team invite field (FURIA, Legacy, Aurora, 9z, BetBoom); Falcons were the only top team to skip the invite round, and PARIVISION and Virtus.pro are not in the announced list.
entries.detail: The event is 16 teams with qualifier slots on top of the announced list. Falcons (and possibly VP) therefore play TWC as their last VRS-ranked event before the cutoff — a rust-vs-rest angle already flagged on the betting guide.

entries.claim: Irregularity: esportbet (Sept 16) called TWC ‘the final opportunity for participating teams to secure VRS points ahead of the Singapore Major’ — but PGL Masters Bucharest ends October 31, before the November 2 VRS cutoff, and includes at least five of the eight TWC teams.
entries.detail: The ‘final opportunity’ phrasing holds only for Falcons (skipped Bucharest) and possibly Virtus.pro. Flagged as irregularity #19; site wording stays ‘one of the last VRS-point opportunities’ (entry 59 for the cutoff).

entries.claim: EPL S24 field verification: all 12 VRS invites were accepted (no declines), and the four ESL Challenger League champions were 1win (the TDK core plus fame and PARIVISION-loanee BELCHONOKK), M80, ShindeN and TYLOO; group seeding was set September 21 and the playoffs run at the Spodek Arena October 9–11.
entries.detail: Entry 50 covers the EPL/TWC clash itself; this adds acceptance status, 1win's composition (connecting entries 51 and the PARIVISION loan web) and the seeding date. HLTV on Aug 10: the top-5 VRS at the time were ‘Spirit, Falcons, 9z, MOUZ, Vitality’ — 9z's slide since is the field's biggest rank move.

entries.claim: No outright market for TWC 2026 existed in the checked betting sources at the fourth-pass check (Sept 24, 2026): esportbet's TWC hub still shows ‘Odds for the Thunderpick World Championship are not available’, and esportsinsider's odds feed carried no futures even for the completed Global Qualifier.
entries.detail: esportbet (Sept 16): top-rated CS2 bookmakers ‘have yet to open outright markets … which should become available closer to the tournament kickoff’. Its hub also mixes 2025/2026 headings — use it as an odds index only. Market types it lists for TWC: outright winner, match H2H, map/kill props, player of the tournament.

entries.claim: Broadcast talent for the Finals is still TBA: Liquipedia lists host, interviewer, analyst, commentator and observer all ‘TBA’ (checked Sept 24); English is the only stream language listed so far. The broadcast runs on twitch.tv/thunderpicktv, kick.com/thunderpick and YouTube.
entries.detail: Production-side uncertainty cannot be priced yet; channels and the language gap are confirmed on Liquipedia and the official release.

entries.claim: Prize distribution is split 50/50 between players and club at every placing: 1st $500,000 ($250,000 player share + $250,000 team share), 2nd $250,000 ($125k/$125k), 3rd $100,000 ($50k/$50k), 4th $50,000 ($25k/$25k), 5th–6th $30,000 ($15k/$15k), 7th–8th $20,000 ($10k/$10k).
entries.detail: Liquipedia's prize table gives the per-place player/team columns; HLTV's event page shows the $500,000 player-share header. Player-share math matters for roster disputes and stand-in cuts under the rulebook's payout rules (entry 47).

entries.claim: The official event site's partner logos include HLTV, Dexerto, VRL and GRID (operator GAM3RS_X; GRID is also the data partner).
entries.detail: Source-independence disclosure: this hub uses HLTV as a primary source and HLTV is a listed event partner — cross-checks against Liquipedia, Valve's GitHub and primary org announcements are therefore mandatory, and are applied throughout the ledger.

entries.claim: Thunderpick is both the title sponsor and a crypto-betting operator (the official site advertises BTC, ETH, LTC, USDT, XRP and BCH payments) whose own markets cover the event it sponsors; TWC is among the largest bookmaker-backed CS2 prize pools.
entries.detail: The rulebook (section 2.9, entry 47) bans players and staff from betting. For readers: treat sponsor-hosted content as marketing rather than analysis, and compare prices across books.

entries.claim: FISSURE Playground 3 (Sept 8-13, Suzhou, $1,000,000, 16 teams) - the last completed event with Finals teams before TWC - ended with Legacy champions, BetBoom 3rd-4th, FURIA 5th-6th, and both 9z and PARIVISION eliminated at 9th-12th; Falcons, Aurora and Virtus.pro did not attend.
entries.detail: Legacy swept G2 3-0 in the final (Ancient 13-9, Mirage 13-10, Dust2 13-4). FURIA lost their quarter-final 0-2 to G2 (Ancient 14-16 in OT after leading 11-7; Dust2 3-13) and had also lost to Legacy in the group stage. BetBoom topped their group 3-0 and lost the semi-final 1-2 to G2. 9z fell 1-2 to G2 in an elimination match (Dust2 13-11 won; Ancient 8-13; Inferno 10-13). PARIVISION lost 0-2 to magic (Ancient 11-13; Inferno 14-16 in OT after leading 12-6) and, per HLTV, 'continue their slide down the rankings'.

entries.claim: BetBoom swept their FISSURE Playground 3 group (2-0 over BIG, 2-0 over Astralis - the organization's first-ever win over the Astralis tag - and 2-0 over MIBR) into the semi-finals, and S1ren called the event 'a ramp-up' for a roughly 20-day European trip (EPL S24 in Katowice, then TWC in Malta).
entries.detail: S1ren (Sept 10): 'We're using this tournament as a ramp-up, because literally in about twenty days we're heading off on a big trip through Europe.' He cautioned that group-stage form does not predict playoffs - BetBoom went 3-0 in groups in Guangzhou earlier in the season and 'just got smashed' in the playoffs there.

entries.claim: FalleN (Sept 12, after FURIA's FPG3 quarter-final exit): 'I know it's coming to an end, and I want to make the most of it' - the 35-year-old's end-of-2026 retirement looms over FURIA's season, and he described the travel grind of going 'from Paris to Porto and then China'.
entries.detail: FURIA also lost to Legacy in Suzhou ('They have been playing very good Counter-Strike'). On the 0-2 defeat by G2: 'I guess we had to win the first map to actually have a chance in the series.' His retirement was originally announced on the IEM Rio stage in April 2026.

entries.claim: YEKINDAR (Sept 16, StarSeries media day) described FURIA's 2026 as title-free despite grand-final appearances at IEM Krakow and the IEM Cologne Major, said the team held a no-conflict meeting after the G2 loss, and framed the FalleN retirement pressure as 'everyone's individual responsibility to be the best version of themselves'.
entries.detail: FURIA's two 2026 grand finals verified in the article: IEM Krakow and the IEM Cologne Major (0-3 vs Falcons). YEKINDAR on the team talk: 'Guys, we know FalleN is going to be retiring; we know we're playing bad right now. How can we fix it? That's basically the mojo.' He also admitted the back-to-back event schedule 'definitely hits you'.

entries.claim: FURIA AWPer molodoy (HLTV #6 player of 2025) is playing through an eye condition that requires surgery: he posted photos of a swollen eye before EWC (reported Aug 9-11), and per the Sept 20 StarLadder broadcast he has pressure behind his eyes causing migraines, with tablets having little effect and surgery planned once he returns to Kazakhstan.
entries.detail: HLTV's StarSeries EVP piece (Sept 23): 'There is more pressure on KSCERATO to deliver with molodoy's eye issues.' Watch item for TWC: any absence would reshape FURIA's ceiling, and the 3-of-5 core-roster rule (entry 41) limits replacements. Sources are an HLTV article, a specialist news post and an X post citing the broadcast - flagged accordingly.

entries.claim: KSCERATO claimed the top EVP of StarSeries Fall 2026 (1.26 rating, 89.9 ADR) despite FURIA not reaching the final - his fourth consecutive event above a 1.20 rating, including a 1.23 rating against top-10 teams while his highest-rated teammate managed 0.97.
entries.detail: HLTV credits him with seven standout maps, 'only two fewer than ZywOo', with big map wins against MOUZ and MIBR.

entries.claim: ZywOo earned an uncontested StarSeries Fall MVP - his fifth of 2026 (1.50 rating, +6.13% round swing) - as Vitality beat Aurora 3-1 in the final for their first title since May, resetting the benchmark the TWC field is measured against.
entries.detail: ZywOo: 'I wanted at least one MVP for the second part of the season... So now it feels good to have this MVP.' ropz added an EVP (1.28 rating in map wins).

entries.claim: Aurora's Jimpphat was the second-best player of StarSeries Fall: a series-high 1.36 rating in the upper-final win over Vitality, a 1.41 rating in map wins en route to the final, and his first EVP since IEM Rio at the end of 2024 - 'Recently I've just had such a crazy amount of confidence.'
entries.detail: Aurora's run: 2-0 over NAVI, 2-0 over NRG, 2-1 over Vitality in the upper final, then a 1-3 grand-final loss to Vitality. HLTV credits coach ash with 'making good on his promise to make him a star anchor once more'.

entries.claim: The FISSURE Playground 3 EVPs went to Legacy's n1ssim (1.20 rating; in the MVP race before the final), G2's NertZ (1.22 playoff rating; first EVP since IEM Rio 2024) and MIBR's nqz (1.21) - and HLTV notes n1ssim had benched himself in the summer, returning only after Legacy failed to replace him.
entries.detail: latto took the MVP (entry 90). n1ssim's award is Legacy's second individual honor from the event and a marker of their top-heavy-but-deep form.

entries.claim: latto (Legacy) is a three-time MVP in China - CAC 2025, CAC 2026 and FISSURE Playground 3, all three of Legacy's Chinese titles - and rated the FPG3 grand final (1.67 rating; a 2.25-rated Dust2) as the best performance of his career: 'It's China magic, I think.'
entries.detail: With two MVP medals and two EVP awards in 2026 he is targeting a first HLTV Top 20 appearance after finishing in the 2025 Top 30; he credits mental work with BobZ, adrrr and arT and his partnership with dumau, together since 2021.

entries.claim: Aurora's former head coach Fabre (benched June 29, 2026) was appointed Eternal Fire head coach on September 11, reuniting with jottAAA and soulfly at the rebuilt, now-international Eternal Fire (ranked #47 HLTV / #67 VRS at the time).
entries.detail: Fabre coached the Turkish core from 2022 to 2025 - overseeing Eternal Fire's PGL Major Copenhagen quarter-final and, after the roster's April 2025 move to Aurora, their IEM Cologne Major semi-final run - before being benched in Aurora's July international rebuild.

entries.claim: BC.Game benched electroNic and signed Australian asap (from THUNDER dOWNUNDER) on September 22 - a move that switches the s1mple-Magisk-Senzu-mzinho project (coached by TaZ) from the Europe VRS, where they sat 36th (outside the top-18 Singapore invite zone), to the Asia VRS, where their 1,191 points would currently rank 4th (five Asian invites).
entries.detail: asap reached his first Major (IEM Cologne Major 2026) with THUNDER dOWNUNDER, posting a 1.24 rating in Stage 1 including a 2.04-rated BO1 win over MIBR. Relevant to TWC as ex-Falcons IGL Magisk's team and as an Asia Major-race marker (both ex-MongolZ players Senzu and mzinho stay).

entries.claim: PGL Masters Bucharest's 16-team field was completed on September 13: Nemiga (Europe qualifier; swept B8 3-0 in the final), DENDELE (South America, beating Imperial and Fluxo twice), Liquid (North America) and TYLOO (Asia) joined the twelve VRS invites - including all five attending TWC teams (FURIA, Legacy, Aurora, 9z, BetBoom) plus Spirit, MOUZ, Vitality, FUT, G2, NAVI and The MongolZ.
entries.detail: Bucharest (Oct 24-31, $1,250,000) starts six days after the TWC grand final; its results feed the Oct 5 and Nov 2 VRS snapshots used for Singapore Major invites and Bucharest seeding.

entries.claim: Perfect World confirmed on September 15 that the second Major of 2027 will be hosted in Shanghai, slated for November 22 - December 12, 2027 over four stages with an expected $1.25 million prize pool; the first 2027 Major will be hosted by FiReSPORTS in Buenos Aires, and HLTV previously reported BLAST and ESL won the 2028 Major bids.
entries.detail: Perfect World's second Major after Shanghai 2024 (won by Spirit over FaZe). Calendar context: the PGL Major Singapore 2026 (Nov 25 - Dec 13) remains the immediate horizon for TWC's VRS points.

entries.claim: Esports World Cup 2027 (July 20 - August 1, 2027) keeps CS2's expanded 32-team, $2 million format; its slot distribution is 20 Global VRS invites, 2 North American, 2 South American, 2 Asian and 2 wildcard invites plus 4 spots from the Riyadh open qualifier (July 16-18). EWC 2028 is tentatively scheduled for July 14-30, 2028.
entries.detail: Calendar context: TWC 2026's VRS weight ($1,000,000) feeds invitation standings that reach as far as EWC 2027.

entries.claim: In the Americas VRS race for Singapore Major invites, BESTIA won Circuit X Curitiba Season 3 (Sept 17-20; +204 points, with drop named tournament MVP by Dust2 Brasil) to move joint-10th with Fluxo - just 14 Valve points outside the qualification zone - while paiN slide continued.
entries.detail: BESTIA's first LAN with drop and kauez. paiN, the region's long-time #1, replaced piriajr with Tatu on September 14 (HLTV) amid the pressure. Context for the South American TWC teams (9z, Legacy) and the Major seeding picture.

entries.claim: Complexity ceased operations, announced September 23: founder and CEO Jason Lake departed after 23 years and ownership of the brand reverted to GameSquare; the organization had exited Counter-Strike in August 2025 citing a 'challenging' esports economy.
entries.detail: One of CS's most storied brands: first roster in 2004, 10 official Majors attended (best: 3rd-4th at DreamHack Winter 2013), titles at ESWC 2005, CPL Summer 2006 and ESL Challenger Jonkoping 2024. Lake: 'this is coL 1 signing out of Complexity, after 23 years.'

entries.claim: Brazilian organization ODDIK suspended esports operations indefinitely with immediate effect (September 23), ending their Counter-Strike division; the org entered CS in June 2022, peaked at #28 in the HLTV rankings after PGL Astana 2025, benched diozera and nardes and released the remaining members as free agents.
entries.detail: The second organization-level contraction of the week (after Complexity, Sept 23) and part of the South American scene backdrop behind 9z and Legacy.

entries.claim: Virtus.pro had cratered below 100th on the VRS before their academy rebuild, then broke into the top 30 by winning the Thunderpick Global Qualifier - a run that began with a loss to K27 and continued with wins over BESTIA, K27, FOKUS, HEROIC (2-1) and HOTU (2-0 sweep in the decider); TWC will be VP's first big international LAN since IEM Chengdu 2025, with only b1st and tO0RO remaining from that roster.
entries.detail: HLTV: the run gives VP 'a slim chance to qualify for the Singapore Major'. The rebuild was built around four former academy members plus mir.

entries.claim: Map-pool profiles from HLTV team stats (all maps played June 24 - September 24, 2026): FURIA Nuke 75.0% / Inferno 66.7% / Anubis 0.0%; Falcons Dust2 75.0% and Inferno 75.0% / Ancient 20.0% / Anubis 0.0% / zero Cache maps; Legacy Inferno 100.0% / Nuke 75.0% / zero Anubis maps; Aurora Nuke 100.0% / Ancient 0.0%; 9z Cache 66.7% / Ancient 25.0% / zero Anubis maps; BetBoom Dust2 100.0% / Mirage 75.0% / zero Inferno maps; PARIVISION Ancient 71.4% / Cache 0.0% / Inferno 20.0% / zero Nuke maps; Virtus.pro Ancient 87.5% / Dust2 72.2% / zero Inferno maps (VP's sample includes non-tier-1 opposition).
entries.detail: Veto-relevant inputs for the betting guide. 'Zero maps' means exactly that in the 3-month window (online + LAN) - not a confirmed perma-ban, which is not published. Sample sizes per map are small (roughly 5-18 maps); rates are context, not probabilities.
